items.name: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
items.title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
items.description: Data attribution methods for Language Models (LMs) are typically evaluated using downstream tasks like fact retrieval. However, existing evaluations vary multiple dataset properties simultaneously, making it impossible to isolate exactly why an attribution algorithm fails. To diagnose these failures, we explore the design space of LLM data attribution, with a primary focus on evaluation. items.title: Propose-Filter-Release: Scaling Noise to Typical Sensitivity via Private Filtering
items.description: An estimator can be accurate and stable on typical data, yet sensitive to a few possible records. Differentially private mechanisms commonly scale their noise to the worst-case influence of a single record, which lets these records dictate the noise even when the remaining data would allow far less. items.name: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
items.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
items.description: The Neural Thickets hypothesis posits that pretrained language models lie in dense neighborhoods of task-specific experts in weight space, which random Gaussian perturbations can uncover. We reproduce the reported gains, but show that they do not require this geometric explanation. items.name: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
items.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
items.description: Pixel-space generative Transformers typically use one token per image patch, so capturing finer detail requires more tokens and makes global attention increasingly expensive. We observe that finer detail does not necessarily require more global communication: low-frequency structure benefits from global exchange, while high-frequency detail can be modeled locally. items.name: Luggage re-identification: A study of strategies towards a real-world application
items.title: Luggage re-identification: A study of strategies towards a real-world application
items.description: Luggage re-identification (ReID) is a critical task in video surveillance for forensics, security or border management (suspicious or abandoned luggage recognition), as well as luggage management (lost luggage recovery). It enables the association of observations of the same luggage across disjoint camera views in complex environments such as airports, train stations and border crossing. items.name: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI
items.title: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI
items.description: Extreme weather is forecast days ahead, yet its consequences for agriculture remain hard to predict: a forecast says where a storm will strike, not which crops will suffer or how much is at risk, and the records that could tell span many sources. items.name: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning
items.title: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning
items.description: World models can achieve strong control performance without faithfully capturing the dynamics of their environment, limiting their potential for mechanistic interpretability and scientific discovery. items.name: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
items.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
items.description: An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. items.name: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
items.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
items.description: Safety alignment has enabled large language models to reliably refuse harmful requests directly, yet the same request distributed across a multi-turn conversation still succeeds far too often. This brittleness has a mechanistic root: Alignment is shallow, with safety behavior concentrated in a model's first few output tokens, and existing defenses inherit the weakness, supervising the surface form of the response without ever giving the model an explicit safety decision to learn. items.title: Testimony from Timelines: Evidence-Grounded Significance Testing of Temporal Clinical Hypotheses
items.description: Ask a language model whether sales tend to dip after a product recall, or whether one side effect tends to follow another after a vaccine, and it answers in a fluent sentence that reads like a finding, with no test behind it. items.title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
items.description: The marginals of a continuous diffusion model can be reproduced by a deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE), known as the probability flow ODE, which provides a foundation for accelerated sampling and consistency distillation. items.title: Difficulty Calibration Across Time for Membership Inference in Diffusion Models
items.description: Modern diffusion models are trained on massive datasets that often include copyrighted or private images. Membership inference attacks (MIAs) address this by testing whether a given image was in a model's training set. items.name: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
items.title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
items.description: We present TextSeal2, a distortion-free watermark for large language models that keeps its signal under speculative decoding: tokens that replace rejected drafts remain watermarked with the same keys, and the acceptance rate is unchanged. items.name: When to Assist and What to Suggest: Joint Gating and Memory-Grounded Hint Generation in One Compact Decoder
items.title: When to Assist and What to Suggest: Joint Gating and Memory-Grounded Hint Generation in One Compact Decoder
items.description: Proactive assistants offer short, memory-grounded hints during a conversation, deciding when to assist and what to suggest. Current systems split this between a gate and a larger generator; we evaluate both together on 28,058 decision points. Stage-wise generation scores are oracle-gate ceilings: behind a real gate, end-to-end exact match is 0.2619 against a ceiling of 0.2971, and end-to-end precision is 0.2387, leaving substantial headroom. items.name: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
items.title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
items.description: An autonomous research laboratory could conduct an entire study, from formulating questions to preparing manuscripts. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers one route towards this goal. Recent AI systems take on several research roles, but may draw conclusions that the evidence does not support. items.title: Multistatic ISAC with Deep Learning-Based Clutter Suppression for 5G and Beyond
items.description: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems using 5G and beyond signals of opportunity enable joint wireless sensing and communication using shared infrastructure and spectrum resources. items.description: Building and scaling computer-using agents (CUAs) across desktop, mobile, and web environments requires reliable task-completion verification for data curation, evaluation, and reinforcement learning. items.title: Multi-View MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation
items.description: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models expand parameter capacity by activating a small subset of experts per token. items.title: PIVOT: Progressive Intervention via Online Teacher Correction
items.description: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) is limited by sparse outcome-level feedback on hard reasoning tasks: when all rollouts in a group fail, rewards provide no learning signal. items.title: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation
items.description: On-policy Self-distillation (OPSD) has proven effective for post-training large language models by constructing a teacher conditioned on privileged references. items.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
items.description: Realistic, fast robotics simulations could enable large-scale training of embodied AI models that transfer to the real world. However, despite decades of progress, available simulations cover only a narrow range of real-world tasks and physical phenomena. items.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
items.description: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. items.title: FARMS: A Verifiable Foundation for Automated Computational Science
items.description: Automated computational science could accelerate discovery by selecting, adapting and developing numerical methods. items.title: Advancing Clinical Genomic Analysis with a Skill-Centred Agent
items.description: Clinical genomic analysis requires experts to integrate evolving guidelines, databases, and computational evidence. items.description: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. items.title: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents
items.description: Long-context models repeatedly solve closely related retrieval problems. Attention or global retrieval can retain large stores, but each forward pass again searches for what matters.
